summary:
The page opens with the last lines of `model.fit(...)`: `batch_size=64` and `validation_data=(val_input_imgs, val_targets)`. The validation set from p.338 is evaluated after every epoch, which is what lets the checkpoint from p.340 monitor `val_loss`.

Next, the training and validation loss are plotted from `history.history["loss"]` and `history.history["val_loss"]`: a red dashed line (`"r--"`) for training loss and a solid blue line (`"b"`) for validation loss, titled *Training and validation loss*.

**Figure 11.5.** Both losses start around 0.85–0.95 and fall together until roughly epoch 10 (about 0.43). After that the training loss keeps decreasing steadily, to under 0.1 by epoch 50 (with a small bump near epoch 46). The validation loss flattens around 0.36–0.40 for epochs 10–20 and then rises, noisily, to about 0.85 by epoch 50, with dips near epochs 39 and 46.

The authors' reading: *we start overfitting midway, around epoch 25*. (From the plot, the validation minimum looks a little earlier, around epochs 18–20; see review flag.) They then reload the best-performing model according to validation loss, the file `oxford_segmentation.keras` written by `ModelCheckpoint(save_best_only=True)`, and begin a prediction demo: pick `i = 4`, take `test_image = val_input_imgs[i]`, and display it with `plt.imshow(array_to_img(test_image))`. The prediction itself and figure 11.6 (test image plus predicted mask) follow on p.342.

concepts.name: Overfitting
concepts.definition: The model keeps fitting training data better while its performance on held-out data worsens.
concepts.intuition: Memorizing the answers to practice questions rather than learning the subject.
concepts.technical: In figure 11.5 training loss falls to under 0.1 while validation loss rises from about 0.36 to about 0.85.
concepts.significance: Determines which epoch's model should be used.
concepts.example: Around epoch 25 (the authors' reading) the two curves clearly diverge.
concepts.misconception: A rising validation loss does not mean training has failed; the best model is simply earlier.

concepts.name: Best-only model checkpointing
concepts.definition: Saving the model only when the monitored validation metric improves.
concepts.intuition: A 'save game' that is only overwritten by a better score.
concepts.significance: Gives the model used for the prediction demo.
concepts.example: The final epoch-50 model is discarded in favour of the earlier best one.

concepts.name: Training and validation curves
concepts.definition: Plots of loss (or metrics) per epoch on training and validation data.
concepts.intuition: A fever chart of the training run.
concepts.technical: Built from history.history lists; the gap between curves measures generalization error.
concepts.significance: Figure 11.5 is the diagnostic for this model.
concepts.example: Red dashed = training loss, blue solid = validation loss.
concepts.misconception: Noisy spikes in validation loss (e.g. at epochs 39 and 46) are normal with a 1,000-image validation set and do not by themselves signal a bug.

code.title: Plotting training and validation loss
code.original_code:
epochs = range(1, len(history.history["loss"]) + 1)
loss = history.history["loss"]
val_loss = history.history["val_loss"]
plt.figure()
plt.plot(epochs, loss, "r--", label="Training loss")
plt.plot(epochs, val_loss, "b", label="Validation loss")
plt.title("Training and validation loss")
plt.legend()

deeper.title: Reading figure 11.5
deeper.body:
Approximate values read from the printed plot:

- **Epochs 1–10:** both losses fall from about 0.85–0.95 to about 0.43. The model is learning generalizable features.
- **Epochs 10–20:** validation loss plateaus around 0.36–0.40 while training loss continues down to about 0.27. This is the sweet spot.
- **Epochs 20–50:** validation loss rises to about 0.85 with spikes and dips, while training loss falls below 0.1. This is overfitting.

The authors summarize this as overfitting beginning midway, around epoch 25.

deeper.title: How to push the curves apart less
deeper.body: Beyond the book: the usual remedies seen earlier in the book also apply to segmentation: data augmentation (with the *same* geometric transform applied to image and mask), dropout or weight decay, a smaller model, or a pretrained encoder. Section 11.3 takes the last route to the extreme with the pretrained Segment Anything Model (p.342).

misconceptions.claim: Because training loss keeps going down, more epochs would help.
misconceptions.correction: Validation loss is what matters for generalization; it rises after the midpoint.

questions.question: In figure 11.5, what indicates overfitting?
options: Training loss decreasing while validation loss increases
Validation loss lower than training loss at epoch 1
questions.answer: Training loss decreasing while validation loss increases
questions.explanation: Divergence of the curves is the signature of overfitting. Both decreasing means it is still learning; rising training loss would signal an optimization problem; the epoch-1 ordering is irrelevant.

questions.question: Which model is loaded by keras.models.load_model("oxford_segmentation.keras")?
questions.answer: The model from the epoch with the lowest validation loss, saved by ModelCheckpoint(save_best_only=True).
questions.explanation: The text says we reload our best-performing model according to validation loss.

questions.question: What do 'r--' and 'b' mean in the plotting code?
questions.answer: Red dashed line and solid blue line.
questions.explanation: Matplotlib format strings: color letter + line style.

questions.question: Why is validation_data needed for the checkpoint callback to work as intended?
questions.answer: save_best_only monitors val_loss, which only exists if validation data is evaluated each epoch.
questions.explanation: Without it there is no val_loss to compare.

questions.question: Looking at figure 11.5 yourself, roughly where is the validation loss lowest, and how does that compare to the authors' 'around epoch 25'?
questions.answer: Around epochs 18–20 (about 0.36); by epoch 25 it is already rising (about 0.45). The authors' figure is a rough 'midway' estimate.
questions.explanation: Read from the plot; the checkpoint would pick the actual minimum.

questions.question: Roughly how many gradient steps does each epoch take?
questions.explanation: 7,390 total − 1,000 validation ≈ 6,390, divided by batch size 64 ≈ 99.8, rounded up to 100.

questions.question: Could you name two techniques that might delay the onset of overfitting in this model?
questions.answer: For example: data augmentation applied jointly to images and masks, dropout/weight decay, or using a pretrained encoder.
questions.explanation: Standard regularization approaches from earlier chapters.
